Samuel's directive: the main xenios website outside /research and /care must not be
redesigned, rewritten, or behaviorally modified. Every Research and Care candidate
must pass scripts/acceptance/verify-core-site-protection.mjs before review.
Built by inspecting the repository at baselineSha, not by assumption.

client/src/lib/content.ts (ICP_BY_SLUG) and client/src/lib/careers.ts (CAREERS_ROLES),

hashAlgorithm.name: sha256-lf
$comment: sha256 over the file's UTF-8 content with every CRLF normalized to LF, so the
digest is identical whether the file is read from a CRLF Windows checkout
(this repo sets core.autocrlf) or from `git show <ref>:<path>`.
Values are prefixed 'sha256:'.

or /care. /admin/research and /admin/research/* are deliberately EXCLUDED: they mount
client/src/research/adminx-section.tsx and belong to the Research surface.
'kind' distinguishes a rendered page from a pure redirect, because a redirect's
protected behavior is its target, not its markup.

$comment: Glob patterns for files that must not change. Evaluated as: a changed path is a
violation unless it matches an allowedWriteZone, an infrastructureZone, or a
permittedSeamFile. These globs are the human-readable statement of the same rule;
the gate's decision is made by the zone lists, so the two can never disagree.

$comment: DELIBERATE DECISION, see docs/phase2/CORE_SITE_PROTECTION.md.
Neither the protected site nor a Research/Care feature: documentation and
verification tooling. Nothing under these prefixes is imported by the client
bundle, mounted by the Express app, or served to a visitor, so a change here
cannot redesign or behaviorally modify the main website. Allowing them is what
lets this protection gate exist in the repo without the gate rejecting itself.
NOTE THE SINGULAR/PLURAL TRAP: 'scripts/' (plural) is tooling and is allowed;
'script/' (singular) is the production BUILD (script/build.mjs, referenced by
package.json's build and render-build) and stays PROTECTED in protectedPaths.
DELIBERATE DECISION, see docs/phase2/CORE_SITE_PROTECTION.md.
Test files pass the gate but are always REPORTED, wherever they live, including
inside the Research and Care write zones.
Why they pass: a test is never bundled or served, so it cannot redesign or
behaviorally modify the website. Refusing them would fire on ordinary Research
work (origin/main's own persistent-cart change touches
server/release-control-plane.test.ts) and would push people to widen this
manifest, which is the one move that defeats the whole mechanism.
Why they are still reported: the repo rule 'do not lower existing safety or
regression gates to make a build pass' is exactly the risk a silent test edit
carries. Review must confirm each touched test was strengthened, not weakened.
This is also what covers server/core-site-protection.test.ts itself: it sits
beside server/release-control-plane.test.ts because that is the repo's existing
home for acceptance tests (vitest.config.ts includes server/**/*.test.ts, and
tsconfig.json excludes **/*.test.ts from `npm run check`), and it is admitted by
the same rule as every other test rather than by a special case for itself.
The ONLY protected files a Research or Care candidate may touch, and only for a
minimal integration seam (registering a route, mounting a router, adding a flag).
Every edit here requires ALL of:
1. an exclusive lease on the file for the duration of the change,
2. the minimum possible diff (a registration line, not a refactor),
3. a focused regression test proving no unrelated behavior moved,
4. QA confirmation that the diff contains no unrelated change.
The gate PASSES a seam edit but REPORTS it, so review never sees one by accident.

shared layout and navigation, the two slug sources the sitemap is pinned to, the
public SEO files, the main server route table, and the build config. A mismatch is
an unconditional FAIL, because none of these can be part of a legitimate

accidental edit, not a lockfile.

2026-08-09, EA HARDENING FUSION, FINAL COMPOSITION: server/index.ts
REVIEWED AND ACCEPTED. Two hunks, both for the customer payment-proof door,
which is the last step of the Early Access journey and was built, tested and
registered nowhere.
(1) IMPORTS: createProofBodyErrorHandler and isProofUploadPath from the proof
route module, EARLY_ACCESS_PROOF_CONTENT_TYPES and TRANSIENT_PROOF_MAX_BYTES
from the modules that already own those constants. Nothing is restated.
(2) A NARROW RAW UPLOAD SEAM. The proof door takes a file, not JSON, so it
needs the raw bytes and a larger ceiling than the site's JSON limit. This is
a MIDDLEWARE ORDER CHANGE and is recorded as one: an express.raw parser is
mounted BEFORE the global express.json, and a scoped error boundary AFTER
both body parsers. It is the narrowest form this server can express:
- the gate is isProofUploadPath, the door's OWN anchored regex over the
exact /api/research/early-access/cart/<XEC number>/payment-proof shape,
so no other path and no path below it enters the parser;
- POST only;
- ONLY the four already-reviewed proof content types, so anything else
falls through unparsed and the door answers its own 415;
- 8 MB, and ONLY there. The global express.json limit is UNCHANGED at 2mb.
It is a predicate middleware rather than app.use(path, ...) because a mounted
path is a PREFIX match, which would have admitted every future path under
.../payment-proof/, and rather than app.post(...) because that would be a
second registration of a path the Early Access API already registers and the
route-uniqueness gate would rightly refuse it.
NO GENERAL req.rawBody RETENTION was added: the raw parser sets req.body for
this path alone and the door hands those bytes straight to validation and to
the internal email attachment. Nothing is written down.
WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: helmet and CSP, the /kairos proxy, request correlation,
the duplicate-slash collapse, trust proxy, session setup, static serving, the
global error handler, the API 404 guard, and every non-research non-care
registration. No guard weakened, no flag changed, no /research access
broadened (the wall already admits this exact path, method-exact, and
server/research/index.ts is UNCHANGED and still matches its baseline). Care
untouched.
THE DOOR IS ALSO CONDITIONAL BEYOND THIS FILE: it mounts only inside the
cart feature flag AND only when the DURABLE proof dependencies were supplied
by the Early Access persistence root, so a deployment that cannot persist a
submission has no door rather than one that forgets. Route cardinality moved
348/339 to 349/340, MEASURED, and the pin was moved to the measured value.
Covered by server/research/early-access/proof/mount.test.ts, which composes
an app in THIS file's order and pins the near-miss paths the predicate must
keep out, the unchanged 2mb JSON limit, the JSON 413 and 415 shapes, and the
door's absence without the durable dependencies.
